evidence: Verg. A. 6.202; Ov. H. 10.65 (Lewis & Short: “to move gently along a smooth surface, … to slide, slip, or glide”)
terms.comment: The classical verb for gliding, said of snakes, ships and birds; Traupman uses it of skating on rollerblades. Standing on the bike, stāns lābitur. See also slip.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
